description:
The usa.gdt dataset (103 quarterly US macroeconomic observations) is loaded in Gretl. It contains: 'lc' (log real personal consumption), 'ly' (log real disposable income), 'inf' (quarterly inflation rate), and 'i' (interest rate).

Your task: Conduct a full VAR (Vector Autoregression) analysis to study the dynamic relationships between inflation and the interest rate. Specifically:
1. Select the optimal lag order for a VAR(p) model of 'inf' and 'i' using information criteria (AIC, BIC/SBC, HQC)
2. Estimate the VAR model at the selected lag order
3. Test Granger causality in both directions: does 'inf' Granger-cause 'i'? Does 'i' Granger-cause 'inf'?
4. Generate impulse response functions (IRFs) showing how each variable responds to a one-standard-deviation shock in the other
5. Save all results (lag selection, VAR estimates, Granger tests, IRF output or description) to /home/ga/Documents/gretl_output/var_macro_results.txt

The dataset spans quarterly US data; the time series structure is already configured.

metadata.data_source: Hill, Griffiths, Lim - Principles of Econometrics 5th ed, US quarterly macroeconomic data
